basis: All five soft-gated runs learned gate probabilities above0.5 for WRITE and below0.5 for DISTRACTOR, yet failed long-delay recall. Direct hard-gate training failed baseline competence in four of five seeds.
question: Does the already learned soft gate's residual distractor updating explain the long-delay failure, rather than failure to separate WRITE from DISTRACTOR?
intervention: Load each soft-gated checkpoint into the existing hard_gated forward rule with exactly the same numerical weights. Use threshold0.5 (already specified in the earlier hard-gate arm), no tuning or retraining. Replay the observations from an empty state.
evaluation: Identical delays0/4/16/64/128, stateoff/on, depths1/2/4/8, earlycue/overwrite/nocue cases. Count fixed weights before/after and hash the source checkpoint.
limits: This changes the state transition algorithm, NOT the weights. It is not a silently compatible serving revision. It diagnoses this discrete token task; it does not establish robust gating for ambiguous observations, language or noisy sensors. Reuses inspected pilot data, so cannot be reported as a fresh confirmatory test. Earlier failures remain in the report.
